title: "Resources"
order: 124
---

This module introduces no new regulation, standard, or framework, and no new source was fetched
for it. It takes a single already-locked fact — the eQMS's (electronic quality-management
system's) own POA&M (plan of action and milestones) entry — and translates it for two audiences
without changing what it says. The links below are the direct inputs this module draws on; read
any of them for the actual mechanics, citations, and reasoning this lesson references by name but
doesn't redevelop.

- **[POA&Ms and
  CAPAs](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/poams-and-capas/index.qmd)**
  (`grc-frameworks-and-risk-management`) — where the exact POA&M entry this module translates was
  built, field by field, from NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2's Task A-6, and placed next to a CAPA
  (corrective and preventive action) to show the same tracking discipline in two vocabularies.
  Read it for the verbatim NIST text and the full reasoning behind every field this module quotes
  unchanged.

- **[Coaching your QA and reporting
  upward](../../directing-the-quality-analyst/coaching-and-reporting-upward/index.qmd)**
  (`directing-the-quality-analyst`) — where the "watermelon report" problem and the discipline of
  separating system measures from personal performance measures were first built, and where a
  management-review packet was first rebuilt around trend and aging instead of raw counts. This
  module's audience-translation instinct is the same discipline, aimed sideways instead of upward.

- **[Building an inspection-ready service catalog and
  CMDB](../building-an-inspection-ready-service-catalog-and-cmdb/index.qmd)** — this course's own
  module 4, which first showed that a self-identified, actively-managed gap grades differently
  than one a reviewer finds cold. This module's exec-quality-council translation leans directly on
  that same point.

- **[Key Performance Indicator (KPI) and Key Risk Indicator (KRI)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BMuP__lM4CY)**
  (ERM Academy, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A professional
  enterprise-risk-management training channel explaining how a KPI differs from a KRI. General ERM
  content, not blood-specific; use it to sharpen which kind of measure you are actually handing an
  executive. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-55 Vol. 1, Measurement Guide for Information Security: Identifying and Selecting
  Measures](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/55/v1/final)** — NIST's own guidance on choosing
  security and risk measures that support decisions. Read it when deciding which measure belongs on
  an executive page at all, before worrying about wording. Not cited by this lesson; background
  only. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[DORA: software delivery performance metrics](https://dora.dev/guides/dora-metrics-four-keys/)**
  — the DORA research program's definitions of change failure rate, recovery time, and related
  measures, the closest public relative of "change success rate" and MTTR. Read it to see how a
  recognized body defines these terms before you report them upward. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: Common incident management metrics](https://www.atlassian.com/incident-management/kpis/common-metrics)**
  — a practitioner explainer showing that MTTR is used for several different intervals (repair,
  respond, resolve), so you must define it before an executive reads it. Vendor-published, so read
  it as industry explainer, not standard. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: What is an SLA?](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/service-request-management/slas)**
  — a plain-language explainer of service level agreements, useful for separating a commitment from
  a measurement before turning an SLA figure into an executive statement. Vendor-published
  explainer, not a standard. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[COSO: Enterprise Risk Management](https://www.coso.org/guidance-erm)** — the Committee of
  Sponsoring Organizations' ERM guidance page, the professional-body home for thinking about risk
  appetite and how risk is reported to leadership. Background for why an executive wants risk
  posture, not raw counts. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NCSC: Cyber Security Toolkit for Boards](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/board-toolkit)** — the
  UK National Cyber Security Centre's guidance on what boards need to hear about cyber risk. UK
  government, not U.S. regulatory; read it for the framing of what executives can act on. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
